subject: Weird geom_point behavior with empty subset

messages.author: 45296ee65ae43883
messages.subject: Weird geom_point behavior with empty subset
parts:
Notice that in the first plot (hwy > 25), the non-empty subset gets
draw as expected.
Unfortunately when the subset is empty all points get colored red. Is
this the expected behavior?

> ggplot(mpg, aes(x=displ, y=cty)) + geom_point(shape=22, colour="black", fill="white", size=1) + geom_point(shape=22, colour="black", fill="red", data=subset(mpg, hwy > 25, size=1))
> subset(mpg, hwy < 0, size=1)
[1] manufacturer model displ year cyl
trans drv cty
[9] hwy fl class
<0 rows> (or 0-length row.names)
> ggplot(mpg, aes(x=displ, y=cty)) + geom_point(shape=22, colour="black", fill="white", size=1) + geom_point(shape=22, colour="black", fill="red", data=subset(mpg, hwy < 0, size=1))


Also, maybe I should be doing this in another fashion. Perhaps:

> mpg2 <- within(mpg, {
+ flg1 <- hwy < 0
+ flg2 <- hwy > 25 })
> ggplot(mpg2, aes(x=displ, y=cty)) + geom_point(aes(colour=flg1))
> ggplot(mpg2, aes(x=displ, y=cty)) + geom_point(aes(colour=flg2))

Is this the proper way to go about what I'm trying to do?

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: Weird geom_point behavior with empty subset
parts:
Hi Tahir,

Yes, I've noticed this bug too. The problem is that when the data is
empty it uses the plot default. Fixing it is on my to do list.

Hadley
